questions.prompt: Which of the following is an exponential function?
hints: The variable is in the exponent.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: An exponential function has the variable in the exponent, like $2^x$.

questions.prompt: The $y$-intercept of the graph of $f(x)=a^x$ ($a>0$, $a\neq 1$) is always ___.
hints: Any nonzero number raised to the 0 power is this.

questions.prompt: The graph of $y=3^x$ is an example of:
hints: Check if the base is greater than 1.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Since the base 3 > 1, the function is exponential growth.

questions.prompt: Solve $5^{x} = 25$ using the One-to-One Property. What is the value of $x$?
What is the equation of the horizontal asymptote for $f(x)=2^x - 3$?
hints: For $f(x)=a^x + k$, the horizontal asymptote is $y = k$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The graph is shifted down 3, so the asymptote is $y=-3$.

questions.prompt: The natural base $e$ is approximately 2.718. To the nearest tenth, $e$ is:
Which formula gives the balance for continuously compounded interest?
hints: Continuous compounding uses the natural base $e$.
The formula involves $e$ raised to the $rt$ power.

questions.prompt: The domain of any exponential function $f(x)=a^x$ ($a>0$, $a\neq 1$) is all ___ numbers.
hints: You can plug in any $x$ value.
There are no breaks or gaps in the domain.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The domain is all real numbers.

questions.prompt: Which transformation describes the graph of $g(x)= -e^x$ relative to $f(x)=e^x$?
hints: The negative sign is in front of the function.
It changes the sign of the output.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Multiplying by $-1$ reflects the graph across the $x$-axis.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is equivalent to $2^{-x}$?
The horizontal asymptote of $f(x)=3^x$ is the line ___.
hints: It is the line the graph approaches but never touches.

questions.prompt: If $\$1{,}000$ is invested at 6% compounded continuously, which of the following gives the balance after 2 years?

hints: Write both sides as powers of 3.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about the function $f(x)=e^{x}$?
options: A. It is decreasing for all $x$.
C. It has a horizontal asymptote at $y=0$.
hints: Recall the graph of $e^x$: it grows to the right and approaches 0 to the left.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: $f(x)=e^x$ has a horizontal asymptote at $y=0$, not at $x=0$.
